text:
Brent just printed $118 and the 10-year Treasury yield is at 4.94%. That relationship used to run the other way .

@robin_j_brooks is correct in this analysis. This is a regime shift, not a blip.

For most of 2026, oil up meant yields up. Inflation expectations fed straight into the long end. That link is now broken. The 20-day correlation between Brent and the 10Y has collapsed to its lowest since late 2024.

The reason is Europe. The French 10-year is at 4.96%, the highest since 2002. The spread over German Bunds has widened to 159bp, the widest since 2011. French debt-to-GDP is 117%, versus 90% at the last crisis peak.

Bessent confirmed this week that capital is leaving "concerning" jurisdictions and flowing into Treasuries as a safe haven. The US is catching a bid because the alternative is worse.

This is not a resolution of the fiscal problem. Net interest is still above $1 trillion. The term premium is being temporarily suppressed by a flight to quality, not by better US math.

If Europe stabilizes, the bid fades. If Europe cracks, the bid deepens.

text:
Binance lost about $6.3 billion in Thursday's hack. It is the largest crypto theft on record in dollar terms, roughly four times the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025.

The drain started at 4:05 PM ET on Oct 29. TRM Labs says most of it left Binance wallets in about 20 minutes, across 10 blockchains.

Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover users. $5 billion of that is already held in the exact tokens that were stolen, about 80% of the loss. It is buying the rest through the market and OTC desks.

About $3 billion has been frozen on-chain, almost all of it $USDT and $USDC. The attacker still holds 18,270 $BTC split across 19 wallets. Elliptic says none of it has reached an exchange or service yet.

TRM and Chainalysis attribute the theft with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit. No government has confirmed it. Trump on Friday: "We don't know. We're looking at that." The FBI and Secret Service are both involved.

TRM counts $12.8 billion stolen by North Korea since 2017. $7.4 billion of it came this year.

Binance is targeting a phased restart of withdrawals early Sunday. Proof of reserves results are due Monday.

"What you are arbing is the exchange counterparty risk, because you're putting funds at risk, and there's a small premium or discount because of that risk."

"To do that trade, you have to have funds on every exchange at all times. Both the token that you're trying to arbitrage and dollars of some sort."

My job is to recognize these shifts in sentiment through price action and technicals, and position myself to ride them.

Whether the market is being rational or irrational, I want to be on the right side of the move.

name: Shay Boloor
zh_summary: StockSavvyShay 認為市場出現錯位：$GOOGL 與 $AMZN 計劃 2027 年進一步加大人工智慧基建支出，市場卻懲罰開支方；他認為基建週期未結束，並計劃繼續加倉高確信的人工智慧電力、推理與代理相關標的。
en_summary: StockSavvyShay argues a dislocation: $GOOGL and $AMZN plan even more AI infrastructure spend in 2027 while the market punishes check-writers; he sees the infrastructure cycle continuing and plans to keep adding high-conviction AI power, inference and agentic names.
text:
I personally think there's a pretty significant dislocation happening in market right now and this week gave me some of clearest evidence yet.

Both $GOOGL and $AMZN are planning to spend even more on AI infrastructure in 2027 after already investing record amounts this year with Andy Jassy even calling AI “a once in a lifetime opportunity” and making it clear Amazon has no plans to slow down.

Putting my corporate strategy hat back on I think market is overlooking something pretty important about Google because it can no longer simply decide AI is getting too expensive and go back to its traditional Search business when AI is now threatening very product that generates most of its profits.

That means infrastructure spending is becoming just as much about defending its existing business as capturing new growth which makes these investments much harder to pull back on even if investors become increasingly concerned about returns.

And that's what makes this selloff so interesting because market is punishing the companies writing the checks while those same companies are telling us they'll write even bigger ones next year.

I absolutely expect next phase of AI to become more selective with clear winners and losers but I don't think that means the infrastructure cycle is ending which is why I plan to keep adding to my highest conviction names across AI power, AI inference and Agentic AI.
